items.title: John Fedchock interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 28, 2015
items.q: Yeah. But what’s interesting with Dizzy, when you hear him play there is so much forethought in what he did.

ctx.x: When I listen to some, any number of people, I think of Dizzy Gillespie sometimes. And sometimes he plays something and I go my God, I never would have thought of that. And it’s until you maybe listen to it again, it didn’t sound right.
Yeah. But what’s interesting with Dizzy, when you hear him play there is so much forethought in what he did. When he does those notes you can hear the intent. It’s not an

accident. And then there’s someone like Miles Davis, who in my mind I think he would intentionally play wrong notes to get his rhythm section to creatively find a way to make something happen. And that’s the thing. If you’re going to play those notes from out of the key or however you want to describe it, you need to have a sensitive rhythm section. If you have someone just banging out the chords — one-three-five-seven-nine — like this, and you play this stuff and they don’t follow you, it’s going to sound wrong,…
